content.text:
I renamed `NamespaceBundle.getNamespaceObject()` to `getNamespaceName()`, but I kept a `getNamespaceObject()` on the class, so it isn't a pure rename. `NamespaceBundle` implements `ServiceUnitId`, which also declares `getNamespaceObject()` (`NamespaceName` and `TopicName` implement it too). Removing it would break the interface contract and the callers typed as `ServiceUnitId`. I left the interface alone because renaming it would force the unrelated `NamespaceName` and `TopicName` to change. `NamespaceBundle` now has `getNamespaceName()` returning `nsname`, plus an `@Override getNamespaceObject()` that delegates to it. I switched every call on a `NamespaceBundle`-typed receiver to `getNamespaceName()`. That covers 9 other files under `src/main` in pulsar-broker:
- `PulsarService`
- `ExtensibleLoadManagerImpl`
- `ServiceUnitStateChannelImpl`
- `TransferShedder`
- `DefaultNamespaceBundleSplitStrategyImpl`
- `NamespaceService`
- `BrokerService`
- `SystemTopicBasedTopicPoliciesService`
- `NamespaceBundleFactory`

Calls on `ServiceUnitId`-typed receivers (`ns`, `serviceUnit`, and `bundle` in `NamespaceService:275` and `ExtensibleLoadManagerImpl:708` and `:746`) still use `getNamespaceObject()`, as do all `TopicName` and `NamespaceName` callers and their declarations. I checked the receiver types by reading declarations, not by compiling, so the later compile check should confirm them. If you want the interface method renamed as well, say so and I'll rename it across all three implementers.
